title: Todd and the Little Green Hook
synopsis: Todd visits from Reed Meadow, sees the first three tiny radish seedlings, and draws them as green hooks and hats.
continuity_state: Before: Five days of seed checking passed without visible shoots. Todd has not visited this garden. Kim and Amy placed two stepping stones with Grandma; sunflower row still bare. After: A few mornings later, about a week or more after sowing, three small radish seedlings have emerged; sunflower row has not visibly emerged yet. Todd visits with Aunt Pat, makes a paper sketch of three sprouts and a yellow boot, takes sketch home. Todd and Amy leave with adults; Kim has not yet been told directly on-screen.

related_resources.reason: University of Minnesota Extension describes radish seedlings emerging within about ten days in suitable conditions; this is a plant observation, not a learning-outcome claim.
Todd represents the visible shoots with imaginative drawing. AAP play guidance is editorial context for playful representation, not evidence of benefits from hearing this story.
